headline: Finland's environment regulator has ordered Google's contractor to halt preparatory work at two planned data center sites until environmental assessments are done.
score_reason: Pool 8 kept: a regulator's order is a real step beyond yesterday's investigation and touches Google's largest European investment of 13 billion euros.
importance_line: Residents and nature groups near Muhos and Kajaani gain a pause on forest clearing, and Google faces delay and possible enforcement, though the halt covers preparatory work, not the whole 13 billion euro plan, and Google says it will follow the agency's guidance.
summary: Al Jazeera reports, citing AFP, that Finland's Supervisory Agency has ordered Tuike Finland, the company acting for Google, to suspend work at planned data center sites in Muhos and Kajaani by 23 Oct 2026, until the environmental impact assessments the law requires are completed. The agency suspects hundreds of hectares of forest were cleared without that assessment; Google acknowledged shortcomings, and the company must explain its next steps by 14 Oct or face enforcement proceedings, a step beyond the investigation we reported in our 6 Oct edition.
notes: Read in full via the Al Jazeera page. The article mixes AFP and Reuters material; the nature-group and Google statements are AFP's. Follow-up of our 6 Oct 2026 edition item on the AFP report of the investigation.
